title: The search that picks a card
summary: Choosing cards in TCG Card Shop Simulator runs through a search with a screen of its own: a scrolling row of cards, a list of what is selected, an empty-slot state and a message for a search that matches nothing valid.
body: Picking a card is a screen rather than a drag. The game keeps a search screen of its own, and it is built from a canvas group with separate parents for the top and the bottom of the row, which is why cards can be presented in a strip rather than a list of names.

What is on show is kept in lists. There is a list of the cards being shown by the search and a further list of those currently active, so the screen knows what is on it rather than reading it back off the objects each time.

What is selected is kept apart. The selected cards have a list of their own, and their displays are moved to a locator as they are chosen, which is why a picked card slides into place instead of jumping.

Selection runs on data, not on pictures. The search carries a list of all card data indices, a list of the ones that are valid for this search and a list of the ones that have been selected, which is how a card can be chosen before anything is drawn.
The row is checked at both ends. The slider's distance is checked on the left and on the right, so the row knows when to stop moving rather than scrolling past its own ends.
It scrolls like a list. There is a current scroll index, a position, a lowest position and a speed for a pad, which is why the same row works with a mouse wheel and with a stick.
An empty search says so. There is a message for a search with no valid card selected, and a list of empty slots for the search, so a failed search is shown rather than looking broken.
What this entry does not tell you: how many cards a search can show, how it decides what is valid, or how far the row scrolls. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The search has a screen of its own with a canvas group and separate parents for the top and the bottom of the row.
The cards on show and the active ones each have a list.
The selected cards have displays of their own, moved to a locator as they are chosen.
Selection is kept as lists of card data indices: all, valid and selected.
The slider distance is checked on the left and on the right.
The row scrolls with a current index, a position, a lowest position and a pad scroll speed.
There is a message for a search with no valid card and a list of empty slots.

alt.en: The game's own card front icons, the small element marks printed on the cards a search shows.
